key_insight: PACEvolve introduces a systematic, progress-aware scaffold for LLM-driven evolutionary search that mitigates long-horizon failures (context pollution, mode collapse, weak collaboration) to keep evolution consistent and improving over many generations.
problem_solved: Unreliable and ad-hoc LLM-in-the-loop evolutionary processes that degrade over long horizons due to history biasing, premature convergence, and poor multi-agent coordination.
method: Progress-aware evaluation: score candidates by measured incremental improvement over recent generations to prioritize genuine progress over superficial fitness.
Context management: prune or summarize experiment history and inject controlled context to prevent past trials from biasing new candidate generation.
Diversity & collaboration mechanisms: enforce diversity-preserving operators and lightweight coordination protocols between agent roles to avoid mode collapse and boost exploration.
impact: Provides practitioners a principled scaffold to run stable, long-horizon LLM-guided evolutionary search, improving reliability and reproducibility of automated design and optimization workflows.

paper_title: PACEvolve: Enabling Long-Horizon Progress-Aware Consistent Evolution
paper_authors: Minghao Yan, Bo Peng, Benjamin Coleman, Ziqi Chen, Zhouhang Xie
